items.title: Pseudo-coherence is local for a finite cover by principal open sets
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pseudo-coherence of a complex can be checked after localising at finitely many elements generating the unit ideal. The proof is an induction on the difference between the highest degree in which cohomology can be nonzero and the bounding degree m: the exactness of localisation identifies the localised cohomology with the cohomology of the localised complex, finiteness of the localised cohomology in the top degree plus the cover lemma gives finiteness of that cohomology module over the ring, and a surjection from a finite free module together with projectivity produces a map to the complex whose cone vanishes in high degrees and whose localisations remain m-pseudo-coherent by the cone lemma, so the induction applies and the cone lemma finishes the argument.
